body:
The parallel `read_csv` path (large local files, default settings) finds the first data row by counting `\n`-terminated lines, but the C tokenizer also ends a line at a bare `\r`. A bare `\r` before the first data row put the first chunk's start in the wrong place, and the existing row-count check missed it whenever the next line was blank or completed a header split by a quoted newline:

```python
"a,b,c\rFIRST,ROW,HERE\n\n" + body        # FIRST,ROW,HERE silently dropped
'a,"line\nbreak",c\rFIRST,ROW,HERE\n' + body  # extra junk first row
```

This falls back to the serial read when the header lines or first data line contain a `\r` not followed by `\n`. CRLF files still read in parallel. No whatsnew: the parallel read is new in 3.1 and not yet released, but it is in 3.1.0rc0, so this should go into 3.1.0.

AI disclosure: drafted with Claude Code (`claude opus 5.5 (high)`), which found the bug by fuzzing and wrote the fix and tests.
title: BUG: parallel read_csv lost or added a row after a bare CR in the header
